skill.name: limrun-expo-development
skill.description: Build and run Expo apps on remote Limrun simulators and emulators, with Metro connections for JavaScript and TypeScript iteration.
skill.summary: Guide Expo development builds, Metro connections, verification, and release previews on Limrun.
skill.author: limrun-inc

security_audit.summary: All 141 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, scoped development commands, expected networking, and a dotenv reference. One semantic finding identifies public Metro exposure in the Expo tunnel fallback without an access-control or consent check. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or malicious reconnaissance.

remediation.issue: The Expo fallback opens a public Metro tunnel without requiring an access-control or consent check.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer private Limrun tunnels. Before public fallback, require informed approval, verify access restrictions, exclude sensitive development data, and stop the tunnel after use.

semantic_findings.title: Public Metro Tunnel Without an Access-Control Check
semantic_findings.description: The fallback instructs agents to start Expo's public tunnel with npx expo start --dev-client --tunnel. It requires no approval or access-control check, so anyone obtaining an unrestricted endpoint could retrieve development bundles and source maps.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback explicitly calls the tunnel public and supplies no access restrictions or approval requirement. Exposure depends on endpoint access and bundle contents.

content.value_statement: Remote Expo development requires matching native builds, Metro routes, and device launch URLs. This skill guides Limrun setup and iteration without rebuilding for every JavaScript change.
actual_capabilities: Guide Expo configuration introspection and derive app identifiers, schemes, branch names, and build asset names.
Check development-client requirements and distinguish reusable Debug assets from builds requiring native updates.
Provide remote Xcode and Gradle build flows with Limrun asset upload and device installation.
Connect Metro through iOS destination tunnels or Android ADB reverse forwarding and construct development-client launch URLs.
Guide verification through TypeScript checks, iOS element trees, app logs, and Android screenshots.
Provide Release build and Limrun preview-link workflows for demos that do not require Metro.
limitations: Requires an Expo project, configured Limrun access, and the relevant development tools.
Detailed build flags and device management depend on companion skills that are not included in this package.
Provides workflow instructions only; it includes no executable automation, native binaries, or test runner.
Targets remote simulators and emulators, not physical-device validation or app store deployment.

output: The ADB tunnel port changes after reconnecting.

output_examples.input: I need a preview that still works after stopping Metro.
output: Use a Release build instead of the Debug development client.
Upload the platform-specific build asset and prepare its Limrun console preview link.
The preview uses the Release asset and does not require a running Metro process.

best_practices: Check the Expo SDK version and native dependency changes before deciding whether a Debug asset is reusable.
Use explicit device instance IDs and keep Metro ports, tunnel routes, and launch URLs consistent.
Prefer private tunnel routes, require approval before public exposure, and stop development servers and tunnels when iteration ends.
anti_patterns: Reusing a Debug asset after native dependencies or native configuration change.
Treating an empty Android accessibility tree as proof that the app failed to render.
Starting a public Expo tunnel without checking access restrictions and approving development data exposure.

faq.question: Does this skill support both iOS and Android?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents remote Limrun iOS simulators and Android emulators, with different Metro connection methods.

faq.question: Do JavaScript changes require another native build?
faq.answer: Usually not. JavaScript and TypeScript changes iterate through Metro, while native dependency, configuration, or build-setting changes require a new Debug build.

faq.question: Is expo-dev-client required?
faq.answer: The development-build workflow requires expo-dev-client. The skill also documents a separate Expo Go launch option.

faq.question: Can I use local simulators instead of Limrun?
faq.answer: This workflow requires Limrun builds and remote devices. Local ADB is used only through the remote emulator tunnel.

faq.question: What should I check after an Android tunnel reconnect?
faq.answer: Read the new tunnel port and restore ADB reverse forwarding with the new serial. Keep passing the explicit Android instance ID.

faq.question: Can a final preview work without Metro?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented final preview uses an uploaded Release asset and a Limrun console preview link.
